elements.text: A computing device comprising: one or more processors;

a non-transitory computer-readable medium; and program instructions stored on the non-transitory computer-readable medium that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the computing device to perform functions comprising:

while serving as a controller for a networked media playback system comprising a first zone player and at least two other zone players, wherein the first zone player is operating in a standalone mode in which the first zone player is configured to play back media individually:

receiving a first request to create a first zone scene comprising a first predefined grouping of zone players including at least the first zone player and a second zone player that are to be configured for synchronous playback of media when the first zone scene is invoked;

based on the first request, i) causing creation of the first zone scene, ii) causing an indication of the first zone scene to be transmitted to the first zone player, and iii) causing storage of the first zone scene;

receiving a second request to create a second zone scene comprising a second predefined grouping of zone players including at least the first zone player and a third zone player that are to be configured for synchronous playback of media when the second zone scene is invoked, wherein the third zone player is different than the second zone player;

based on the second request, i) causing creation of the second zone scene, ii) causing an indication of the second zone scene to be transmitted to the first zone player, and iii) causing storage of the second zone scene; displaying a representation of the first zone scene and a representation of the second zone scene; and while displaying the representation of the first zone scene and the representation of the second zone scene, receiving a third request to invoke the first zone scene; and

based on the third request, causing the first zone player to transition from operating in the standalone mode to operating in accordance with the first predefined grouping of zone players such that the first zone player is configured to coordinate with at least the second zone player to output media in synchrony with output of media by at least the second zone player.

elements.text: A computing device comprising: one or more processors;
elements.quote: Free Sonos app guides you through setup and provides music control for everyone in the house on all their devices—phones, tablets, and computers.
elements.evidence_summary: The official guide identifies phones, tablets, and computers as devices running the Sonos controller app. It does not expressly identify the processors in those host devices.

basis.reasoning: The guide directly identifies phones, tablets, and computers as controller-app hosts and carries a March 2022 date. The cited passage does not specify a host processor, so the assessment is partial rather than treating ordinary computing-device architecture as expressly documented.

elements.text: a non-transitory computer-readable medium; and program instructions stored on the non-transitory computer-readable medium that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the computing device to perform functions comprising:
elements.quote: Download the app from the app store on your mobile device. Open the app and we’ll guide you through setup.
elements.evidence_summary: The S2 guide instructs users to install and run the controller app locally on a mobile device. It does not expressly describe the non-transitory storage medium or execution of stored instructions by processors.

basis.reasoning: Installation, downloading, opening, and using the S2 app to control the system establish locally running controller software. The passages do not expressly identify a non-transitory medium or processor-execution implementation; those details are therefore left as gaps.

elements.text: while serving as a controller for a networked media playback system comprising a first zone player and at least two other zone players, wherein the first zone player is operating in a standalone mode in which the first zone player is configured to play back media individually:
elements.quote: Saved groups are available on Sonos systems that contain three or more products. Sonos systems with one or two products will not see an option for saved groups.
elements.evidence_summary: Saved-group functionality requires three or more Sonos products, and the user guide separately describes independent room playback. These sources do not establish the particular three-zone-player configuration or the first player’s standalone state during both preset-creation requests.

basis.reasoning: Support requires at least three products for saved groups, the guide describes independent listening, and developer documentation recognizes single-player groups. These are related capabilities, not an explicit account of the specified three-player configuration with the first player remaining standalone during preset creation.

elements.text: receiving a first request to create a first zone scene comprising a first predefined grouping of zone players including at least the first zone player and a second zone player that are to be configured for synchronous playback of media when the first zone scene is invoked;
elements.quote: Select the rooms you want to include in your saved group.
elements.evidence_summary: The saved-group creation workflow accepts the user’s chosen rooms and a group name, then saves that selection as a preset. Sonos’s S2 announcement explains that selecting the saved group automatically groups its players, and its grouping documentation specifies synchronized playback.

basis.reasoning: The creation instructions expressly accept selected rooms and a name for a saved group. The S2 announcement explains invocation and automatic grouping, and grouping support states that grouped products play in sync; together these document the user-facing predefined-group creation behavior.

elements.text: based on the first request, i) causing creation of the first zone scene, ii) causing an indication of the first zone scene to be transmitted to the first zone player, and iii) causing storage of the first zone scene;
elements.quote: If you frequently add the same Sonos rooms together in a group, you can save that group as a preset in the Sonos app. This saved group will show as an option along the top of the Grouping menu.
elements.evidence_summary: The app creates and retains a room-group preset for later selection. The source does not describe transmitting an indication of that saved preset to the first zone player or identify where the preset is stored.

basis.reasoning: Saving a selected room group and making it available for later selection supports creation and retention of the preset. None of these passages specifies transmission of the preset's indication to the first player or the storage location, so the compound element is only partially documented.

basis.reasoning: Plural saved groups and room-selection instructions support creating multiple presets with selected membership. The sources do not expressly show the required first-plus-second and first-plus-third overlapping memberships, which is the stated gap.
